scripts.//prebuild: Refuses to build if a legal document has drifted from its digest, if the pricing page disagrees with the API's packs, or if a page links somewhere that does not exist. npm runs this before `build`, so VERCEL RUNS IT ON EVERY DEPLOY. Both of the first two are factual misstatements to the person least able to check them — a stale privacy policy, and a price the webhook does not charge — which is why they stop a deploy rather than warning.
scripts.prebuild: npm run resolve:release && npm run verify
scripts.verify: npm run verify:legal && npm run verify:pricing && npm run verify:demo && npm run verify:pages && npm run verify:env && npm run verify:release-states
scripts.//verify:demo: The landing page's demo shows the template the grader actually gives out. It is the first VoidCode code a visitor ever sees, and it is a copy because it renders before any request resolves.
scripts.//verify:pricing: The page advertises the prices the webhook actually grants. Checked against src/lib/credit-packs.json, which is the application's exported contract — see scripts/check-pricing.mjs for why this is the most consequential check here.
scripts.//sync: Refresh the copies this repository holds of things the application owns: both legal documents, their digests, and the credit-pack contract. Takes the path to a VOIDCODE checkout; there is no default on purpose.
scripts.//lint:ratchet: Lints and fails only if the problem count exceeds the committed baseline. This repository was extracted with 20 errors that are real, pre-existing and outside the code it was extracted to serve; a blocking lint would make CI red from the first push, and a CI that is always red is one nobody reads. See scripts/lint-ratchet.mjs.
